newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Tyco to buy AT&T submarine cable business.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Tyco to buy AT&T submarine cable business.

text.p: Industrial conglomerate Tyco International Ltd. said Friday it agreed to buy AT&T Corp.'s underwater telecommunications cable business for about $850 million.

The acquisition of AT&T Submarine Systems Inc. (SSI) will broaden Tyco's role in the growing market for fiber optic telecommunication cable. Tyco's Simplex Technologies unit manufactures undersea fiber optic telecommunications cable. The AT&T business makes electronic components that join the cable and also installs, supplies and maintains the systems.

"The combination makes Tyco the world's only fully integrated single source for everything from cable system design to manufacturing to installation and maintenance," Tyco Chairman Dennis Kozlowski said in a news release.
The business, which experienced a slowdown in the early 1990s, now is booming due to the expansion of the Internet and an increase in international phone, fax and data traffic.
Tyco, based in Exeter, N.H., also noted global telecommunication capability is creating demand around the world in areas not currently connected to the undersea cable network.

The acquisition marks the second large deal for Tyco in the past month. Last month, it announced a $5.4 billion acquisition of electronic security giant ADT Ltd., which had rejected a hostile takeover bid from Kansas utility Western Resources Inc.
Tyco said the latest deal would have an immediate positive impact on earnings and provide substantial long-term benefits. It projected revenues for the AT&T unit at about $1 billion in 1997.

AT&T Submarine Systems recently won two major contracts totaling approximately 25,000 kilometers (16,000 miles) of undersea telecommunication cable to be installed by the end of 1998. Much of the cable for the projects is to be manufactured by Simplex.
"The addition of SSI will give us a distinct competitive advantage in the fast-growing global marketplace for undersea telecommunications cable systems," Kozlowski said.

AT&T previously had announced its intent to sell the business and Tyco publicly had expressed interested in buying it. In a statement announcing the sale, AT&T President Officer John Walter said it ensures that AT&T's portfolio includes only businesses key to its communications services strategy.
AT&T Submarine Systems President William Carter, other SSI executives and some 800 employees will join Tyco as part of the deal.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette analyst Jack Blackstock estimated the deal could add as much as 10 cents per share to Tyco's annnual earnings in the first year of the deal.
For the fiscal year ended June 30, 1996, Tyco earned $310 million, or $2.03 per share.
Tyco spokesman David Brownell did not dispute that estimate and said Tyco will continue pursuing transactions in its other business areas.
"Tyco historically continues to do acquisitions. We do them across all segments of our business," he said.
Tyco manufactures disposable medical products, packaging materials, flow-control products, and electrical and electronic components.
Tyco stock slipped 50 cents to $57.75 on the New York Stock Exchange amid broad market losses. AT&T's stock fell 62.5 to $33.875, also on the NYSE.
